edits.location: When the ceremony is in the morning, paragraphs 1 and 2
edits.issue: The 4.30am first chair is arithmetically consistent (2pm to 11am is three hours, 7.30am to 4.30am) but reads as alarming and as a recommendation. Keep it as an example, state the shift rather than the clock time, and lead with the levers, including one the 4pm examples already show (no first look starts the chairs an hour later).
edits.fix:
Replace exactly (occurs once): OLD: "The method is the same, with less room in it. In the 2pm example the first chair begins at 7.30am. Move the ceremony to 11am with the same people and team, and that chair moves to 4.30am.

The answer is more hands, fewer people in the chairs or simpler looks, agreed with your team well ahead. Check sunrise with the calculator above, as the first chairs may need lamps." NEW: "The method is the same, with less room in it. Take the 2pm example, where the first chair begins at 7.30am. Move that ceremony to 11am with the same people, the same team and a first look, and every time in the morning moves three hours earlier with it.

Rather than starting that early, change the shape of the morning and agree it with your team well ahead: a second stylist or artist so more chairs run at once, fewer people in the chairs or simpler looks, and portraits after the ceremony instead of a first look, which in our 4pm examples lets the chairs start an hour later. Check sunrise with the calculator above, as the first chairs may need lamps."

fact_check_log.claim: Geoscience Australia's sunrise, sunset and twilight calculator works these times out using the National Gazetteer of Australia (linked to geodesyapps.ga.gov.au/sunrise at the claim).

You can search a place name or enter a latitude and longitude, including places outside Australia, choose a time zone, and see a single day or a whole year (same sentence pair as the linked tool; marker present).
Bureau of Meteorology forecast link: instruction only ('check ... in the days before'), no claim about BoM.
4pm sample with a first look (9am, 12.30pm, 1pm, 1.45pm, 2pm, 2.45pm, 3.15pm, 3.30pm, 4pm): planning example, framed 'for example', matches wedding-timeline-4pm-ceremony/08-final.md line for line.
4pm sample without a first look (10am, 1.30pm, 2.30pm, 3.30pm, 4pm): planning example, matches the 4pm final.
Intro, photographer H3 and FAQs repeat 9am/10am and 12.30pm/1.30pm as examples: consistent with the samples.
15 minute buffer between the last chair and dressing: planning example matching the 4pm final's buffer section; FAQ wording edited so it no longer claims the sample lists show it.
Morning ceremony: 2pm to 11am is three hours earlier, so 7.30am becomes 4.30am. Arithmetic correct; reframed by edit to state the shift and the levers rather than the clock time.
No per-person hair or makeup duration stated anywhere; durations referred to the stylist and artist and the trial.
Chair order, dressing block, partner's side photographed in turn, getting-ready space, destination questions: planning advice phrased as practice, no factual claim needing a source.
'There is no single honest figure to plan around': research-flavoured claim about available figures.

Wedded Advisor lines: plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world; single point of contact start to finish; works in your time zone; fee agreed in writing before any work begins; confirms inclusions in writing before you commit. All in brand-facts 'Claims we can make'.
